summary.oneLiner: Medanta delivered record Q4FY26 revenue (INR 11,958cr, +25% YoY) and PAT (INR 1,417cr, +40% YoY), driven by robust volume growth and improving realizations, while Noida losses narrowed significantly (INR 236cr in Q4 vs INR 320cr in Q3) signaling an inflection point toward breakeven in H2FY27. The strategic pivot from pure bed-addition to high-throughput procedural capacity (10 new OTs planned) and specialty gaps (oncology, transplants) underpins sustained ARPOB growth and margin resilience despite competitive intensity in Gurugram.
summary.business: Medanta operates advanced tertiary and quaternary care hospitals offering integrated healthcare across 30+ specialties, with hospitals in Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore and Noida. The platform rests on four pillars: advanced multi-specialty hospitals; specialty clinics and outpatient care; diagnostics and clinical support services covering radiology imaging, pathology laboratory services and advanced diagnostic testing; and a continuum-of-care and digital health layer spanning telemedicine, Tele-ICU, retail pharmacy, home healthcare and preventive health programmes. Hospitals bring key specialties under one roof with dedicated specialty floors, integrated inpatient and outpatient services and modular design, serving patients across North, East and Central India.

Medanta Hospital, Ranchi (Abdur Razzaque Ansari Memorial Weavers' Hospital; Medanta SAC Hospital)
Continuum of care and digital health: Home healthcare - ICU-at-home, nursing and clinical care, medical equipment rental, sleep studies
Post-acute bundled care for oncology and transplant patients

currentContext.strategies: Institutionalise quality care by replicating clinical protocols, governance mechanisms and training systems across the network, so that outcomes are consistent across geographies rather than dependent on any single site or clinician.|Expand access through a large greenfield and brownfield bed pipeline - approximately 3,350 additional beds in existing hospitals and across five greenfield locations - targeted at markets where demand is growing but specialised healthcare remains limited.|Take advanced tertiary and quaternary care to underserved regions: Guwahati for the Northeast, Varanasi for eastern Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring regions, and Mumbai and Delhi to deepen presence in two major healthcare markets.|Use public-private and partnership structures to build capacity: the Jay Prabha Medanta Hospital in Patna as the demonstration of what such collaboration can achieve, the proposed Varanasi hospital, the upcoming Guwahati facility, and work with DLF in South Delhi.|Run a doctor-led, multidisciplinary model in which patients access multiple specialties within one institution, with continuity from diagnosis and treatment through rehabilitation and follow-up.|Build a broader continuum of care around the hospitals through clinics, diagnostics, pharmacy, telemedicine and homecare, enabling earlier engagement, structured follow-up and post-discharge support, and connecting preventive care, diagnosis, hospital treatment and recovery into one integrated system.|Advance clinical excellence in high-acuity programmes - robotic surgery, structural heart interventions, CAR T-cell therapy, transplantation and neurosciences - by sustained investment in specialist clinicians, multidisciplinary teams, medical equipment, clinical protocols and supporting infrastructure, and by strengthening existing centres of excellence while developing new specialty programmes and supporting research.|Attract and retain experienced clinicians and develop talent internally: establish the Medanta Institute of Medical Education to support DNB programmes and specialist training, and pursue a proposed Medical College in Gurugram, addressing the shortage of trained professionals.|Adopt technology - artificial intelligence, precision diagnostics, minimally invasive robotics and digital platforms - selectively on the basis of clinical relevance and ability to improve patient outcomes, supported by clinical oversight, data governance and operating protocols.|Grow preventive healthcare alongside hospital capacity through community health programmes, clinical outreach and integrated care services, encouraging earlier diagnosis, regular screening and better chronic disease management.|Develop each new hospital as a comprehensive clinical institution supported by the Medanta Model of Care, rather than as a standalone bed addition.
currentContext.expansion: Medanta's growth agenda is built on scaling capacity at existing hospitals, establishing new facilities in underserved regions, introducing advanced super specialities and investing in clinical expertise and technology. In FY 2025-26 the Company added 623 beds - 382 at the newly launched Noida facility, 131 at Patna and 110 at a newly built hospital in Ranchi - taking total installed bed capacity to 3,665 beds as of March 31, 2026 against 3,042 beds in FY 2025, a 20.48% increase (the Board's Report describes the same year as 500+ beds added, a 20.5% increase). Looking forward, the Company plans to add approximately 490 brownfield beds across its existing hospitals at Indore, Lucknow, Noida and Patna, with a first tranche indicated for Q1 FY27 at Lucknow and Noida, lifting installed capacity to about 4,155 beds in FY27e. In addition it plans nearly 2,950 beds across five greenfield projects over the next three to four years - Pitampura, Delhi (~750 beds), South Delhi (~400 beds, being developed with DLF), Oshiwara, Mumbai (~750 beds), Guwahati (~650 beds) and Varanasi (~400 beds) - which would take capacity to about 7,105 beds and roughly double the network in four years. The Guwahati project follows completion of land acquisition during the year for a proposed 400+ bed multi-specialty hospital in Guwahati, Assam, with planned capacity subsequently enhanced from 400 to 650 beds after a revision in National Building Code norms; the Varanasi project was approved by the Board under a build-to-suit and lease arrangement; Mumbai (Oshiwara) is under construction; and development activities progressed across Mumbai, South Delhi and Pitampura. Separately, in May 2026 the Company entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire an approximately 80-bed cancer hospital in Indore, to be launched during Q2/Q3 FY 2026-27, complementing the existing 175-bed Indore hospital. The total project capex for the ongoing expansion is estimated at approximately Rs 48,500 million, described elsewhere as capex planned for the next five years, and the capex plan also carries lines for maintenance capex, a Medical School and a guest house. Borrowings rose during the year to fund greenfield projects, which the Company cites as the reason its debt-equity ratio rose to 0.16 from 0.1, interest coverage fell to 20.92 from 27.8 and return on capital employed fell to 14.98% from 18.10%, with returns from those investments expected to accrue over future periods. Alongside organic expansion the Company is actively pursuing inorganic growth - evaluating strategic acquisitions, building partnerships and collaborations, entering new geographies and diversifying service offerings.
currentContext.mdna: Rising burden of non-communicable diseases from changing lifestyles, urbanisation and an ageing population; NCDs account for approximately 65% of all deaths in India versus 37% in 1990, cardiovascular disease causes an estimated 28.6 lakh deaths annually, and diabetes affects over 100 million Indians - driving demand for tertiary and quaternary care.|Structural bed shortage: India has only 15 hospital beds per 10,000 population against a global average of 33; North India has just 15-16 beds per 10,000 versus 26-27 in South India, and the North India healthcare delivery market is expected to grow at a 12-14% CAGR from Rs 1.9-2.0 trillion in FY2024 to Rs 3.1-3.2 trillion by FY2028.|India's healthcare delivery market stood at Rs 6.3 trillion in FY 2024 and is projected to reach Rs 9.4-9.8 trillion by FY 2028, a 10-12% CAGR; private providers are expected to account for 69-70% of the market by FY 2028, up from 67% in FY 2024.|Private hospitals are expected to post 14-15% revenue growth in FY 2027, a fifth consecutive year of double-digit growth, supported by healthy occupancy, rising realisations and faster ramp-up of new facilities; corporate hospital revenues have compounded 15-16% over the past five years on a persistent demand-supply imbalance.|Listed hospital companies ran approximately 65% occupancy in FY 2026 with operating margins of 22-24%; private sector revenues are projected to compound 16-18% with ARPOB growth of 6-8%.|Case-mix shift towards high-acuity specialties - cardiology, oncology, neurosciences, gastroenterology and orthopaedics accounted for over 62% of total hospital revenues in FY 2026, up from about 58% pre-pandemic.|New facilities are reaching financial break-even within 12-18 months, far faster than the 3-4 year timeline typical of the previous decade - relevant to the ramp of Medanta's own developing hospitals.|Company performance drivers in FY 2025-26: double-digit revenue growth across all quarters supported by higher patient volumes, improved case mix and operational efficiencies; margin was diluted by start-up costs at the newly commissioned Noida hospital, with EBITDA excluding Noida up 18.6% year-on-year at a 25.7% margin.|International patient revenues grew 33.2% in FY 2025-26 as patients from diverse geographies chose Medanta for specialised and complex treatments.|Pharmacy (hospital and retail) revenue grew 30.4% year-on-year in FY 2025-26; IPD volume rose 16.0% to 202,112.|Expanding health insurance penetration, rising incomes and greater health awareness broadening the addressable base for organised, quality-focused care.|Government policy tailwind: MoHFW allocation of Rs 1,06,530 crore in Union Budget 2026-27, up 10%, the first time India's healthcare allocation has crossed Rs 1 lakh crore; expanded Ayushman Bharat, AI-enabled centres and robotic surgery units, and customs duty exemptions on 17 cancer and rare disease drugs.|Demographic tailwinds, expanding health insurance penetration, the growing appeal of medical tourism, progressive policy reforms and accelerating digital health adoption are each reinforcing the others, creating a compounding structural case for sustained sector growth.|Demand is rising in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities faster than clinical and institutional capability is developing there, creating room for operators able to attract experienced clinicians and maintain consistent standards.|Supply-side competitive backdrop: listed players are expected to add about 15,000 beds over the next few years, entailing a capital outlay of Rs 30,000-32,000 crore.|Pipeline of approximately 3,350 additional beds, comprising expansion in existing hospitals and five greenfield locations.|Approximately 490 beds expected to be added during FY 2026-27 and 2,700 beds over the next three to four years.|Named pipeline projects: Guwahati (650 beds, land acquired), Varanasi (400 beds, Board-approved, build-to-suit and lease), Mumbai (under construction), Pitampura (Delhi), South Delhi (with DLF), and an approximately 80-bed cancer hospital in Indore under a Business Transfer Agreement signed May 2026.|FY 2025-26 delivery against the pipeline: the Chairman's message reports 623 beds added across the network during the year, while the Board's Report states 500+ beds were added, a 20.5% increase in overall bed capacity, taking total operational capacity to 3,665 beds as of March 31, 2026.

risks.risk: Operational risk - occupancy variability against a high fixed-cost base
risks.note: Variations in occupancy levels or an unanticipated increase in fixed operating costs may affect growth and margins. Hospitals carry heavy fixed costs, and network occupancy has been flat at 62% for three years while capacity grew 20.48% in FY 2026, so incremental beds must be filled to protect margins. Mitigation cited is expansion into underserved markets beyond a single-hospital model and a multi-hospital network that diversifies the operating base and reduces dependence on individual facilities.

risks.risk: Expansion / project-execution risk on a bed pipeline larger than the existing network
risks.note: Delays in the planning, construction or completion of new facilities may affect profitability and returns on investment. The Company is committing to roughly 490 brownfield beds and about 2,950 greenfield beds over three to four years at an estimated project capex of about Rs 48,500 million - a programme bigger than the 3,665 beds it currently operates. Mitigation is close monitoring of project timelines, regulatory approvals, construction progress and other critical dependencies to ensure timely commissioning.

risks.risk: Start-up drag from newly commissioned hospitals
risks.note: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 23.4% from 25.4% because of start-up costs at the newly commissioned Noida hospital; excluding Noida, EBITDA rose 18.6% with a 25.7% margin. With a multi-year pipeline of five greenfield hospitals, each new opening imposes a similar reported-margin drag until it ramps.

risks.risk: People risk - dependence on scarce senior clinical talent
risks.note: High attrition, talent shortages or difficulty attracting skilled professionals may affect brand reputation, growth and service quality. The model depends on exclusively associated senior specialists; mitigation is a differentiated doctor engagement model, integrated HR systems covering recruitment, structured training and retention, performance-linked compensation and a structured appraisal system, and hospitals positioned as destinations for specialised care.

risks.risk: Patient and staff safety risk, managed outside the formal (non-medical) risk framework
risks.note: During FY2025-26 the Company identified 'Safety Risk to Patients, Staff or any other personnel' as a Key Risk. Notably, the formal group risk assessment covers only Non-Medical Risks; medical risks are managed separately by the Quality Departments of each unit under NABH and JCI norms, with accreditation audits forming the review. Mitigation is adherence to JCI and NABH standards and clinical safety protocols, regular audits, monitoring, timely corrective action and patient-safety culture training.

The hospitals in Patna, Indore, Ranchi and Noida are dependent on leased land, which could put operations at risk if lease agreements are breached - four of six operating hospitals. Mitigation cited is long-term contractual tenure, including a 27-year lease for Indore and a 90-year lease for Noida.

Instances of legal non-compliance, adverse publicity, substandard service quality or patient dissatisfaction may adversely affect brand perception. In a business where clinical reputation and JCI/NABH accreditation drive patient choice, this is a direct revenue risk. Mitigation is governance practices, transparent operations and continued focus on patient safety.

risks.risk: Competitive risk in the healthcare services market
risks.note: Intensifying competition may pose challenges in attracting skilled professionals and sustaining occupancy levels. Mitigation cited is the hospitals' established position as destinations for specialised care backed by clinical quality, and a diversified presence across five states that supports patient inflows including from neighbouring states.

Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications: failure to manage emissions may lead to elevated greenhouse gas emissions, regulatory non-compliance, adverse impacts on the health of employees, patients and surrounding communities, reputational challenges and higher operating costs. Mitigation is monitoring of Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions and increasing adoption of renewable energy across operations.

The BRSR materiality table flags inadequate risk management as a material risk with negative implications - exposing the organisation to financial, operational and reputational challenges including data breaches, regulatory penalties and business disruptions, and hindering crisis response and recovery. Mitigation is comprehensive periodic risk assessments plus contingency plans and response protocols. The framework itself is still extending with the footprint: the group-wide assessment covered 29 functions and the risk-management function was only rolled out at the newly opened Noida unit during FY2025-26.

financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 11,958cr (+25% YoY); EBITDA (ex-Noida): INR 3,142cr (+27% YoY, 27.5% margin); PAT: INR 1,417cr (+40% YoY, 11.8% margin); Order Book: N/A (Service sector, replaced by Pipeline: 2,700 beds over 3-4 years); Net Debt: Net Cash INR 5,906cr. One-offs/Distortions: Noida early-stage operating loss (INR 236cr in Q4) drags consolidated margins by ~320bps; Corporate costs fully loaded on Gurugram unit artificially suppressing its standalone margin profile; ESOP expenses excluded from reported EBITDA.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth expected driven by volume & realization; Margin: Mature units stable at 24-25%, Developing units (ex-Noida) >30%; Order Inflow: Strong international funnel activation; Capex/Commissioning: INR 45,000cr over 5 years for 2,700 new beds; Noida breakeven expected in H2FY27.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline includes 400-bed Varanasi (build-to-suit), 400-bed Guwahati (land acquired), South Delhi (diaphragm wall complete), Mumbai & Pitampura (regulatory stage). Total planned addition: ~2,700 beds via 5 greenfield projects over 3-4 years plus ~500 beds via brownfield expansion.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mature (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi): Rev INR 7,257cr (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,935cr (+15% YoY, 26.7% margin). Developing ex-Noida (Lucknow, Patna): Rev INR 3,728cr (+33% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,207cr (+42% YoY, 32.4% margin). Noida: Rev INR 525cr, EBITDA loss INR 236cr (improving from INR 320cr in Q3), occupancy ~30%.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Specialty gaps closure in Noida (Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Liver Transplant) and Patna (Lung Transplant, Chest Surgery); 2) Procedural capacity addition (10 new OTs across network including Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna); 3) International market recovery (Middle East, Bangladesh) + new markets (Africa, CIS, SE Asia); 4) Oncology expansion in Indore (80-bed acquisition).
margins & cost dynamics: Mature margins compressed slightly (40bps FY26) due to employee cost inflation, offset by material cost optimization. Q4 mature margins recovered to 26.7% (+100bps YoY). Corporate overhead fully allocated to Gurugram. Management confident in sustaining 24-25% mature margin range via scale benefits and tariff hikes (CGHS full-year impact).
capex / expansion: Total project capex guidance INR 45,000cr over 5 years. FY26 saw commissioning of Noida (550 beds), Ranchi (110 beds), Patna expansion (131 beds). Near-term capex focused on MEP/fit-out for Varanasi (lease model) and OT/ICU expansions in existing units.
capital allocation: Net cash position INR 5,906cr; Operating cash flow INR 7,144cr (FY26). Final dividend INR 0.50/share (25% of face value). Strategy favors internal accruals + project-specific debt for greenfield; active M&A/O&M exploration (recent Indore acquisition) for inorganic growth.
risks & watch-items: 1) Competitive intensity in Gurugram (2 new competitor hospitals opening soon) potentially impacting doctor retention/pricing; 2) Slower-than-expected Noida ramp-up (occupancy ~30% vs breakeven ~40-45%); 3) Geopolitical tensions affecting Middle East patient inflows; 4) Regulatory delays in greenfield projects (Mumbai, Pitampura).
management quality / tone: Confident and pragmatic; emphasized 'procedural capacity' over mere bed count as key growth lever; acknowledged wage inflation but highlighted operational efficiencies (ALOS reduced to 3.04 days); reiterated discipline in M&A and strong clinical value proposition to retain talent.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly shifted narrative from 'bed occupancy' to 'procedural throughput' (OTs, Cath labs) as the primary constraint and growth driver, noting ALOS reduction (3.76 days in FY22 to 3.04 in FY26) masks true volume growth. Noida's early hiring of senior clinicians was framed as a deliberate P&L hit to secure long-term clinical depth, differentiating its ramp-up from pandemic-era launches (Lucknow/Patna).

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Medanta operates advanced tertiary and quaternary care hospitals offering integrated healthcare across 30+ specialties, with hospitals in Gurugram, Lucknow, Patna, Ranchi, Indore and Noida. The platform rests on four pillars: advanced multi-specialty hospitals; specialty clinics and outpatient care; diagnostics and clinical support services covering radiology imaging, pathology laboratory services and advanced diagnostic testing; and a continuum-of-care and digital health layer spanning telemedicine, Tele-ICU, retail pharmacy, home healthcare and preventive health programmes. Hospitals bring key specialties under one roof with dedicated specialty floors, integrated inpatient and outpatient services and modular design, serving patients across North, East and Central India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising burden of non-communicable diseases from changing lifestyles, urbanisation and an ageing population; NCDs account for approximately 65% of all deaths in India versus 37% in 1990, cardiovascular disease causes an estimated 28.6 lakh deaths annually, and diabetes affects over 100 million Indians - driving demand for tertiary and quaternary care.
- Structural bed shortage: India has only 15 hospital beds per 10,000 population against a global average of 33; North India has just 15-16 beds per 10,000 versus 26-27 in South India, and the North India healthcare delivery market is expected to grow at a 12-14% CAGR from Rs 1.9-2.0 trillion in FY2024 to Rs 3.1-3.2 trillion by FY2028.
- India's healthcare delivery market stood at Rs 6.3 trillion in FY 2024 and is projected to reach Rs 9.4-9.8 trillion by FY 2028, a 10-12% CAGR; private providers are expected to account for 69-70% of the market by FY 2028, up from 67% in FY 2024.
- Private hospitals are expected to post 14-15% revenue growth in FY 2027, a fifth consecutive year of double-digit growth, supported by healthy occupancy, rising realisations and faster ramp-up of new facilities; corporate hospital revenues have compounded 15-16% over the past five years on a persistent demand-supply imbalance.
- Listed hospital companies ran approximately 65% occupancy in FY 2026 with operating margins of 22-24%; private sector revenues are projected to compound 16-18% with ARPOB growth of 6-8%.
- Case-mix shift towards high-acuity specialties - cardiology, oncology, neurosciences, gastroenterology and orthopaedics accounted for over 62% of total hospital revenues in FY 2026, up from about 58% pre-pandemic.
- New facilities are reaching financial break-even within 12-18 months, far faster than the 3-4 year timeline typical of the previous decade - relevant to the ramp of Medanta's own developing hospitals.
- Company performance drivers in FY 2025-26: double-digit revenue growth across all quarters supported by higher patient volumes, improved case mix and operational efficiencies; margin was diluted by start-up costs at the newly commissioned Noida hospital, with EBITDA excluding Noida up 18.6% year-on-year at a 25.7% margin.
- International patient revenues grew 33.2% in FY 2025-26 as patients from diverse geographies chose Medanta for specialised and complex treatments.
- Pharmacy (hospital and retail) revenue grew 30.4% year-on-year in FY 2025-26; IPD volume rose 16.0% to 202,112.
- Expanding health insurance penetration, rising incomes and greater health awareness broadening the addressable base for organised, quality-focused care.
- Government policy tailwind: MoHFW allocation of Rs 1,06,530 crore in Union Budget 2026-27, up 10%, the first time India's healthcare allocation has crossed Rs 1 lakh crore; expanded Ayushman Bharat, AI-enabled centres and robotic surgery units, and customs duty exemptions on 17 cancer and rare disease drugs.
- Demographic tailwinds, expanding health insurance penetration, the growing appeal of medical tourism, progressive policy reforms and accelerating digital health adoption are each reinforcing the others, creating a compounding structural case for sustained sector growth.
- Demand is rising in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities faster than clinical and institutional capability is developing there, creating room for operators able to attract experienced clinicians and maintain consistent standards.
- Supply-side competitive backdrop: listed players are expected to add about 15,000 beds over the next few years, entailing a capital outlay of Rs 30,000-32,000 crore.
- Pipeline of approximately 3,350 additional beds, comprising expansion in existing hospitals and five greenfield locations.
- Approximately 490 beds expected to be added during FY 2026-27 and 2,700 beds over the next three to four years.
- Named pipeline projects: Guwahati (650 beds, land acquired), Varanasi (400 beds, Board-approved, build-to-suit and lease), Mumbai (under construction), Pitampura (Delhi), South Delhi (with DLF), and an approximately 80-bed cancer hospital in Indore under a Business Transfer Agreement signed May 2026.
- FY 2025-26 delivery against the pipeline: the Chairman's message reports 623 beds added across the network during the year, while the Board's Report states 500+ beds were added, a 20.5% increase in overall bed capacity, taking total operational capacity to 3,665 beds as of March 31, 2026.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Medanta's growth agenda is built on scaling capacity at existing hospitals, establishing new facilities in underserved regions, introducing advanced super specialities and investing in clinical expertise and technology. In FY 2025-26 the Company added 623 beds - 382 at the newly launched Noida facility, 131 at Patna and 110 at a newly built hospital in Ranchi - taking total installed bed capacity to 3,665 beds as of March 31, 2026 against 3,042 beds in FY 2025, a 20.48% increase (the Board's Report describes the same year as 500+ beds added, a 20.5% increase). Looking forward, the Company plans to add approximately 490 brownfield beds across its existing hospitals at Indore, Lucknow, Noida and Patna, with a first tranche indicated for Q1 FY27 at Lucknow and Noida, lifting installed capacity to about 4,155 beds in FY27e. In addition it plans nearly 2,950 beds across five greenfield projects over the next three to four years - Pitampura, Delhi (~750 beds), South Delhi (~400 beds, being developed with DLF), Oshiwara, Mumbai (~750 beds), Guwahati (~650 beds) and Varanasi (~400 beds) - which would take capacity to about 7,105 beds and roughly double the network in four years. The Guwahati project follows completion of land acquisition during the year for a proposed 400+ bed multi-specialty hospital in Guwahati, Assam, with planned capacity subsequently enhanced from 400 to 650 beds after a revision in National Building Code norms; the Varanasi project was approved by the Board under a build-to-suit and lease arrangement; Mumbai (Oshiwara) is under construction; and development activities progressed across Mumbai, South Delhi and Pitampura. Separately, in May 2026 the Company entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire an approximately 80-bed cancer hospital in Indore, to be launched during Q2/Q3 FY 2026-27, complementing the existing 175-bed Indore hospital. The total project capex for the ongoing expansion is estimated at approximately Rs 48,500 million, described elsewhere as capex planned for the next five years, and the capex plan also carries lines for maintenance capex, a Medical School and a guest house. Borrowings rose during the year to fund greenfield projects, which the Company cites as the reason its debt-equity ratio rose to 0.16 from 0.1, interest coverage fell to 20.92 from 27.8 and return on capital employed fell to 14.98% from 18.10%, with returns from those investments expected to accrue over future periods. Alongside organic expansion the Company is actively pursuing inorganic growth - evaluating strategic acquisitions, building partnerships and collaborations, entering new geographies and diversifying service offerings.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Brand and clinical reputation: Medanta - Gurugram was ranked No. 1 hospital in India in Newsweek's 'World's Best Hospitals 2026' and has featured among the world's best for seven years in a row
- Large-format single-campus scale: Gurugram is the largest single-location private hospital in the network with 1,440 operational beds and all key specialties under one roof, enabling the 'Medanta Model of Care' for managing complex disease through multidisciplinary collaboration
- Regional leadership positions - largest private hospital in Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow), largest private hospital in Patna, second-largest private hospital in Ranchi
- Demonstrated high-acuity clinical capability across cardiac sciences, neurosciences, oncology, transplants, foetal medicine and peripheral vascular sciences, including India's first EVOH embolisation for a high-flow arteriovenous malformation and CyberKnife radiosurgery
- Accreditation depth (JCI, NABH, NABL) supporting quality assurance and payer empanelment; Noida secured NABH within six months of commencing operations
- Integrated ecosystem beyond inpatient care - clinics, labs, pharmacy, home care and digital health - creating a continuum of care around the hospital network
- Capital-efficient entry routes into new geographies: long-term leases (Indore 27-year, Noida 90-year, Ranchi 15-year), a 33-year concession agreement in Patna, an O&M arrangement for the new Ranchi unit and a build-to-suit lease for Varanasi
- Founder-led clinical institution founded by Dr. Naresh Trehan, recipient of the Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri and Dr. B.C. Roy Award
- A matured base funding the build-out: Gurugram, Indore and Ranchi together carry 1,925 beds of capacity and are the network's matured hospitals
- Institutional validation of the platform through prior minority investments by the Carlyle Group and Temasek, and the subsequent IPO listing on BSE and NSE

other.body:
- [Acquisition] Indore Cancer Unit — an 80-bed cancer hospital being added under a business transfer agreement, announced April 2026, to be operationalized in Q2/Q3 FY27.
- [Regulatory] A revision in National Building Code (NBC) norms allowed Guwahati's planned bed capacity to be increased from 400 to 650 beds, and lifted that project's stated capex to INR 9,700 million.
